Series::traverse_put_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::traverse_put_(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec> specs, const Series& values) -> Series&

What It Does¶

Writes into the current series through a selector that must remain view-representable, mutates in place, and returns *this.

This is the strict write-side companion to traverse_slice(). It uses selector syntax, but it does not accept the full extract() surface. Its contract is intentionally narrower:

  • destination selection must be representable as an ordinary view traversal

  • after that selector check passes, writing follows the usual scalar-broadcast or exact-cardinality rules

So traverse_put_() is best when you want selector-based writes, but you also want the API to reject anything that would require materializing scattered positions.

Parameters¶

specs (pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>)

The destination selector.

Accepted selectors are the same view-representable subset used by traverse_slice():

  • scalar indices

  • positive-step slices

  • SliceAll()

  • Ellipsis

  • NewAxis

Rejected selectors include:

  • negative-step slices

  • boolean masks

  • integer advanced index series

  • mixed selectors that require materialized advanced indexing

NewAxis is still permitted because it is view-like bookkeeping rather than a materializing index operation.

values (const Series&)

The source data to write into the selected region.

Two value modes are accepted:

  • scalar broadcast

  • exact element-count replacement

Like the broader selector-write surfaces, values is converted to the target dtype and platform if necessary before assignment.

Returns¶

Series& The same series, after mutation.

Examples¶

Example 1. A whole-column write is accepted because the destination is plainly view-representable.

auto grid = pluss::make_series(
    std::vector<double>{10, 11, 12, 13, 20, 21, 22, 23, 30, 31, 32, 33},
    {3, 4});

auto col_values = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{100, 200, 300}, {3});
const std::vector<ExtractSpec> middle_column{
    pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(),
    std::int64_t{1}};

grid.traverse_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(middle_column),
    col_values);

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, 100, 12, 13],
  [20, 200, 22, 23],
  [30, 300, 32, 33]]

Example 2. Scalar broadcast still works after the selector passes the stricter view-only validator.

const std::vector<ExtractSpec> row_tail{
    std::int64_t{2},
    pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(2, 4, 1)};

grid.traverse_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(row_tail),
    pluss::codem::value(-5.0));

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, 100, 12, 13],
  [20, 200, 22, 23],
  [30, 300, -5, -5]]

Example 3. A reverse slice is rejected here even though the broader extract_put_() surface could have handled it.

try {
  const std::vector<ExtractSpec> reverse_specs{
      pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(),
      pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(-1, pluss::Slicing::Slice::kUnbounded, -1)};

  grid.traverse_put_(
      pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(reverse_specs),
      pluss::codem::value(0.0));
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

Series::traverse_put_: selector is not view-representable; use extract() or extract_put_() for materializing paths

This is the key boundary of the method: it is not “write through any selector,” it is “write through a selector only if that selector is still a pure traversal.”

Notes¶

  • traverse_put_() is the strictest selector-write method on Series.

  • Use it when you want the API to guard against accidental advanced indexing.

  • If the selector needs reverse traversal, masking, or integer gather-style addressing, move to extract_put_().

  • If you want value semantics instead of mutation, use traverse_put().

See Also¶

  • Series::traverse_put: copy-returning version with the same selector gate.

  • Series::traverse_slice: read-side companion.

  • Series::extract_put_: broader write surface that accepts materializing selectors.
